newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity rallies on cash, natgas, SW heat.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity rallies on cash, natgas, SW heat.

text.p: NYMEX electricity finished sharply higher Friday, underpinned by strength in the West physical power prices, a rebound in natural gas futures and ongoing hot weather in parts of the Southwest.
"A lot of people just want to own it," said one Houston futures trader.
Market sources said there was keen buying interest today from western utilities to cover their June deliveries.
June Palo Verde (PV) futures settled at the day's high at $20.75, up $1.15 a megawatt hour (MWh).
July PV ended up 84 cents at $24.60. Deferred PV ended 10 to 69 cents higher.
June California-Oregon Border (COB) settled up 65 cents at $15.00. July COB finished up 50 cents at $16.80. Other COB months ended down 20 cents to up 40 cents.
Firm, peak Monday power prices at COB were little changed at $16.25-17.50, while those at PV climbed to $19.50-21.00 from $19.25-20.00.
Daily cash prices remained buoyant by reduced hydropower supply in the Northwest and generation tightness in the Southwest, market sources said.
Hydropower availability in Northwest is reduced due to flood control measures in effect in British Columbia, and Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) is limiting daily offers for peak demand hours.

About 4,000 megawatts (MW) of generating capacity in the Southwest is said to be currently offline for repairs or maintenance, although much of that capacity was expected to return to service later this month.
A 550 MW unit at the Jim Bridger coal-fired generating complex in Wyoming was expected to return to service Friday after being shut almost two weeks ago for repairs.
NYMEX June Henry Hub natgas futures settled up 2.4 cent at $2.267 per million British thermal units, erasing an early 4.3 cent loss.
In the Southwest, fair, dry weather is expected across the region with readings running near normal in the northeast to four degrees above normal in the southwest into next week.

In the Pacific Northwest, temperatures would average near normal in the northeast to about two degrees Fahrenheit below normal southwest, with a chance of scattered precipitation this weekend, forecasters said.
NYMEX estimated 332 COB and 630 PV contracts were sold, compard with Thursday's 414 COB and 1,014 PV lots.
